parameters.content:
## A personal video of the cart they walked away from

Cart-recovery email number three gets ignored. This one carries a
1080x1920 video of **their** items: a hook scene that says their first name
over their own product photo, a line-up of the 1-3 things still in the cart
with prices, then the cart total and a "complete your order" card.
~14-15 s, rendered by Zvid, optionally mailed to them by this same workflow.

**No Shopify store needed to try it.** `source` is `sheet` out of the box, so
a Google Sheet with one row is a complete working demo. Flip `source` to
`shopify` when you want it watching real abandoned checkouts - see the
*Production path* note further down.

### Setup (about three minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** - create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** - attach your Google credential to *Read carts sheet*
   and *Mark cart recovered*, then pick your spreadsheet + tab in BOTH nodes.
   The expected columns are in the note below.
3. **Open `Config`** - set `brandName`, `storeUrl` and the `hookLine` /
   `ctaText` copy. Colours and fonts live there too.
4. **Run it - the first run renders for real and spends about 15 credits.**
   When it finishes, click **▶ Watch video** to play the reel here in n8n.
5. Free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config**: you get the credit
   quote plus an **editorLink** to watch the draft, nothing spent, the sheet
   untouched and no email sent. Set it back to `false` to render.
6. Optional email: set `sendEmail: true` and attach an SMTP credential to
   *Send recovery email* (see the note near it).
7. **Activate** - it takes one cart per run, hourly.

## Your carts sheet: fourteen columns

Header row (row 1), spelled exactly like this:

| Email | FirstName | Item1 | Item1Image | Item1Price | Item2 | Item2Image |
| Item2Price | Item3 | Item3Image | Item3Price | CheckoutUrl | Status | VideoUrl |

- **Item1** is the only required cell. `Item2`/`Item3` are optional and the
  layout is designed for all three counts: one item gets a tall hero card,
  two get deep rows with big thumbnails, three get a tighter stack.
- **Item*Image** - public http(s) URLs (Shopify CDN links are). A missing or
  non-http image is replaced by a designed numbered tile, never a broken box.
- **Item*Price** - write them however your store does (`128`, `128.00`,
  `$1,049.00`, `49,00`). The builder reads the number, keeps your formatting
  on screen and adds the items up for the cart total. One unreadable price
  and the total line is replaced instead of shown wrong.
- **Email** - used ONLY to send the recovery mail. It never reaches the video
  or the video URL (see the Privacy section of the note near that node).
- **FirstName** - optional. Empty just drops the name line from the hook.
- **Status** - leave EMPTY for carts waiting to be recovered. The workflow
  takes the first empty-Status row and writes `done` + the video URL when the
  render lands. Put anything in Status by hand to skip a row.

A sheet with only the header row, or a row where every cell is blank, is not
an error: *Pick next cart* skips blank rows and *Nothing to recover* ends the
run with a friendly line telling you what to add.

## Production path: real abandoned checkouts

**Shopify has no abandoned-checkout webhook topic.** There is no event to
subscribe to, so this polls - which is also the install with no app review,
no public URL and no Shopify Trigger node:

*Poll checkouts* asks `GET /admin/api/{apiVersion}/checkouts.json?limit=25`
every hour. That endpoint only ever returns checkouts that were **never
completed**. *Pick abandoned checkout* then applies the window: older than
`abandonedAfterHours` (6 - give them a chance to come back on their own) and
younger than `maxAgeHours` (48 - a two-week-old cart is not a recovery
opportunity), must carry an email and at least one line item, and must not
already be in the sent-list. Oldest qualifying cart wins.

### The token (about two minutes)

1. Shopify admin -> **Settings -> Apps and sales channels -> Develop apps**
2. **Create an app**, then **Configure Admin API scopes** and tick
   **`read_checkouts`** (add `read_products` only if you want product images).
3. **Install app**, then reveal the **Admin API access token** (`shpat_...`).
   It is shown once - copy it now.
4. Add a SECOND n8n **Header Auth** credential: name
   `X-Shopify-Access-Token`, value = that token. Attach it to *Poll
   checkouts* only.
5. In **Config** set `source: "shopify"` and `shopDomain` to the full host
   (`your-store.myshopify.com`).

In Shopify mode there is no sheet row, so the write-back is skipped and the
checkout id is remembered in the workflow static data instead - that is what
stops the same cart being recovered twice. It is stored only AFTER a
successful render, so a failed render retries the same cart.

`/checkouts.json` does not reliably carry product images; the numbered-tile
fallback is what you will see when it does not.

**A rejected poll stops the run instead of pretending the store is quiet.**
*Pick abandoned checkout* reads the HTTP status: 401/403 says the token or
the scope is wrong, 404 says shopDomain / apiVersion is wrong, anything else
non-200 is quoted back. Only a real 200 with an empty window ends in
*Nothing to recover*.

## The layout is designed for 1, 2 and 3 items

A cart automation that only looks right at two items is a cart automation you
cannot switch on. *Build project JSON* measures and re-composes:

- **One item** - a single tall card, big product photo on top, name and price
  under it.
- **Two items** - deep rows with 380 px thumbnails.
- **Three items** - tighter rows with 250 px thumbnails and a longer scene
  so all three still land before the cut.

The card block always starts under the rule and finishes near the same
baseline, so no count leaves the frame half empty.

**Product names shrink, then ellipsise.** A greedy wrap estimate calibrated
against the production renderer steps a title down through its size ramp
until it fits its card in at most three lines, and only then cuts on a word
boundary with an ellipsis. A 147-character title cannot spill out of a card.

**Prices keep your formatting.** `$1,049.00` stays `$1,049.00`; a bare `249`
becomes `$249`. Cents appear on the total only when the store itself quotes
cents, so `$128.00 + $42.00` totals `$170.00` and not `$170`.

**Their own photo is the backdrop** - blurred and dimmed behind the first two
scenes. No stock footage to go stale, and the palette always matches the
product. With no usable photo the frame draws halo rings instead.

## Free preview: the optional dry run

**`dryRun` is `false` in Config, so a run renders for real.** Set it to
`true` whenever you want a free pass instead: the workflow validates the
payload, quotes the exact credit cost and saves the project as a **draft**,
then reports an **editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the exact video and tweak anything by hand, with nothing
spent. On a dry run **the sheet row is not marked done and no email goes
out**, so the next real run picks the same cart.

Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render, mark the row and send.

## The recovery email, and what leaves your n8n

`sendEmail` is **false** by default - the template renders and reports, and
sends nothing until you opt in. To switch it on:

1. Add an n8n **SMTP** credential and attach it to *Send recovery email*.
   Gmail needs an **App Password**, not your account password.
2. Set `sendEmail: true` and `emailFrom` in **Config**.

The subject and intro live in Config as `emailSubject` / `emailIntro` and
support `{firstName}`, `{brandName}`, `{total}` and `{itemCount}`. They are
substituted in *Prepare recovery email* (a code node, where escaping is easy
to get right) so the mail node itself has nothing to debug.

The step **continues on error**: a bad SMTP password never costs you a
finished render, and `emailSent` in the run summary tells you what happened.

### Privacy

This workflow handles customer email addresses, so two things are
deliberate:

- **The email address never touches the video.** The finished MP4 sits on a
  public CDN, and the CDN filename comes from the project `name`. That name
  is built from the **first name only** plus a hash of the cart contents -
  `cart-alex-vtnk1j9q`. Anyone who guesses a URL learns a first name, not a
  customer record.
- **The address is used once, to address the mail.** It travels from the
  sheet (or the Shopify checkout) to *Send recovery email* and stops there.
  It is not written to the video, the payload or the project title.

Everything else stays inside your n8n instance. If you would rather your ESP
own the send, switch `sendEmail` off and pass `videoUrl` to Klaviyo /
Mailchimp / Braze instead (see the note to the right).

## Delivering it (optional tail)

The required path ends with the URL in *Run summary* (and in the sheet), plus
the built-in SMTP send. To go further, extend after *Run summary*:

- **Klaviyo / Mailchimp / Braze** - push `videoUrl` into a cart-recovery flow
  as a custom property and let your ESP own timing and deliverability. This
  is the production swap most stores want; the SMTP node is the zero-setup
  demo.
- **SMS / WhatsApp** - the URL is short and public; pass it to Twilio.
- **Retargeting ads** - drop `videoUrl` into your ad platform via its API.

They stay out of the required path so the import runs with a Zvid key and a
Google account, nothing else.

### ▶ Watch video

Click the last node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button - the finished reel, no URL to copy.
*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (plus `jobId`,
`creditsCharged`, `cartTotal`, `emailSent`) if you want to pipe the result
onward.
